top_categories.workout_context: Race-pace efforts that mimic Gran Fondo Il Lombardia's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before October.

Road-specific control matters at Gran Fondo Il Lombardia. Practice on paved — Italian provincial and municipal roads: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 67 miles.
117ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Gran Fondo Il Lombardia, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
7,874ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
7,874ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Gran Fondo Il Lombardia. Train it until it feels boring.
67 miles on paved — Italian provincial and municipal roads burns energy faster than the distance suggests. Train the fade resistance now.

Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on paved — Italian provincial and municipal roads can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Gran Fondo Il Lombardia. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Low-cadence force work supports 7,874ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 7,874ft of climbing on paved — Italian provincial and municipal roads does to your power file on race day.
